# ---- the pointers where these objects' code works them out ----
# the objects these functions start, in A6 from their callers (find_free_object): their fields by the new kind's
# family (the writes 00FD2E "ori.b #$80, ($2f,A6)", 010342 "ori.b #$80, ($2f,A6)", 0107FA "move.b #$1, ($2f,A6)",
# 010B14 "move.l A5, ($20,A6)", 010D9A "move.l A0, ($20,A6)")
param hydrant_start_water a6 water object.hydrant_water
param billboard_start_soldier a6 soldier object.billboard_soldier
param turret_start_shot a6 shot object.turret_shot
param nozzle_row_start_nozzle a6 nozzle object.freeze_nozzle
param electric_vent_start_column a6 column object.electric
# the vent the column tells it is gone (010E1E "movea.l ($20,A0), A6", 010E22 "move.b #$1, ($2f,A6)")
local electric_column_leave 010E1E a6 vent object.electric


# ======== the rock soldiers and their shots (01154E-012A2D) ========
# The two bosses made of rock (kinds 1E and 1D) and the objects their code starts. What each kind is comes from its
# code, its spawn records (area_spawn_lists: +6 the kind, +7 the parameter) and its animations, rendered from the
# addresses its set_animation calls take; nothing in the program names the two bosses, so they go by their areas. Their
# stats come from set_object_stats' 10-byte records (+0 attack and hit, +2 health_bars, health and damage, +6 depth, +8
# the hit sound). "Struck" is routine 4, which the attack check sets on an object a turtle's attack hits
# (0472CE "move.w #$400, ($4,A1)"); "gone off the screen" is flags bit 5 (remove_if_off_screen). The turtles they look
# for are the first four objects whose player is in play and not out (0600A1 and not 0600A0) and that are not being hit
# (routine 4: 011AE4 "btst D6, $600a1.l", 011AEE "btst D6, $600a0.l", 011AF8 "cmpi.b #$4, ($4,A6)").
#
# kind 1E rock_soldier_site: the boss of area 7, the building site (one spawn record, 05F10C, at height 0x80): a big
#   humanoid of rock with a gun (rendered: 014E52 aims it). He drops in from above once the scroll reaches 0x6E000,
#   lands shaking the screen to the boss music and "Crash the turtles!", then walks at a turtle, stands or jumps
#   (landing with the screen shaking), strikes a turtle close by, and fires bursts of gun blasts (kind 34) at a turtle
#   in front within 0x8C. He takes 40 hits (his stats' bars) and 2 more for each player in play
#   (011588 "move.b ($8,A0), ($24,A0)", 0115A6 "lsl.w #1, D7"); every hit takes one. No scenario reaches him (index.txt:
#   0 ran).
# kind 1D rock_soldier_technodrome: the boss of area 8, the Technodrome (one spawn record, 05F3DE): a rock soldier with
#   a missile launcher (rendered: 01548A, a missile fired from it, the launcher's smoke ring). Unseen until the scroll
#   reaches 0xD1000, he appears with the boss music, a wall slab (kind 48) flying off and the shock bars (kinds 4C and
#   4D); then walks at a turtle, stands or taunts (speech A6, or B1 "Crash the turtles!"), strikes a turtle close by,
#   and fires a missile (kind 49) at a turtle in front at least 0x46 away. He takes 40 hits and one more for each player
#   (0121E6 "add.b D7, ($24,A0)"). The scenario area8 beats him.
# Both: struck, a flinch (or, with no hits left, the defeat: 10 explosions, then four pieces of rubble, kind 41, fall
#   off him and he stays as a heap of rocks: rendered 014F9E and 015672); his colour flashes more as he weakens. Kind 1E
#   runs his own moves (011C0E) and 1D his (012452) from the shared code by the kind (0119CE "cmpi.b #$1e, ($2,A0)"), so
#   the static analysis sees both kinds reach both.
# kind 34 gun_blast: kind 1E's gun blast (01186C starts it: 011FD2 "move.w #$3400, ($2,A6)"): 0x48 in front of him at
#   height 0x30, it flies at 0x400 for its animation's 22 frames (rendered 014FC2: a small blast that swells into a
#   burst), attack 0B (turtle_hit's table at 01C272 has the same reaction for 0A and 0B); it tells the soldier when it
#   hits. No scenario runs it.
# kind 41 rubble: a piece of rock that falls off a defeated rock soldier (011A78 starts four:
#   0120BA "move.w #$4100, ($2,A6)") and stays on the ground (rendered 0151BA, 0151C4, 0151CE: lumps of rock, by the
#   parameter)
# kind 48 wall_slab: a big slanted slab (rendered 0156DE) that flies off left at 0x800 as kind 1D appears, knocking
#   turtles flying (attack 07); as it starts a block of 6 by 17 tiles is drawn into a layer (0126DA "lea $191a4.l, A6",
#   0126E4 "jsr $183fa.l") (012668 starts it: 01266E "move.w #$4800, ($2,A6)")
# kinds 49 and 4A missile: kind 1D's missile (rendered 01569A: a missile with its flame; 012716 starts kind 49:
#   01271C "move.w #$4900, ($2,A6)"), which flies at 0x300 knocking turtles flying (attack 87) and explodes against a
#   wall or outside 0x60-0x17F across on the screen; a turtle can hit it out of the air. Kind 4A has the same routines
#   (the table at 0126FE) and no spawn list, record or code starts it.
# kind 4C shock_bars: three tall posts in a row (rendered 015752: white bars) that appear with kind 1D, 0x8A nearer the
#   front than him (012894: 01289A "move.w #$4c00, ($2,A6)", 0128AC "addi.l #$8a00, ($16,A6)"), blinking faster and
#   faster until they flicker on, until he is defeated, then blinking slower and slower until they are gone; they do not
#   attack
# kind 4D shock_bars (hit box): not drawn, the bars' picture with its attack box (0129B4 "movea.l $1574e.l, A6"), at
#   kind 1D's place as he appears (012984: 01298A "move.w #$4d00, ($2,A6)"): while the bars flicker on it attacks one
#   frame in 16 with attack 0A, which electrocutes a turtle (the electric beam's attack, kind 30)
#
# Two routines no path reaches are named here (0116A2, 0129C0): the analysis takes them from their func lines.
# 06130B and 06130C, which 0123F8 and 012830 test, are never set by any code
# (the only writes clear 06130B: 01221C, 012856), so the missile's limit they would make never applies.

# ---- the families' fields ----

# the hits it still takes: its bars from its stats plus 2 for each player in play (kind 1D: plus 1) at its start
# (011588 "move.b ($8,A0), ($24,A0)", 0115A8 "add.b D7, ($24,A0)", 0121E6 "add.b D7, ($24,A0)"); each hit one less, the
# last one defeats it (01190E "subq.b #1, ($24,A0)", 011912 "beq $1195a"); its flashing goes by it
# (011F5C "cmpi.b #$1c, ($24,A0)", 011F68 "cmpi.b #$14, ($24,A0)", 011F74 "cmpi.b #$a, ($24,A0)")
scoped object rock_soldier 24 hits_left u8
# the blows it struck since its last hit, up to 3 (011D04 "addq.b #1, ($26,A0)", 011D12 "move.b #$3, ($26,A0)",
# 011936 "clr.b ($26,A0)"): with the turtles in play they pick the blow's animation, slower as they go
# (011CEC "add.b ($26,A0), D7", 011CF0 "move.b (A6,D7.w), D7") and the chance of the next one
# (0116F6 "move.b ($26,A0), D1")
scoped object rock_soldier 26 blows u8
# frames after it recovers before it can be hit again (0119C0 "move.b #$8, ($2a,A0)", 011F4E "subq.b #1, ($2a,A0)",
# 011F56 "ori.b #$2, ($0,A0)")
scoped object rock_soldier 2A hit_delay u8
# the players in play at its start (0115A2 "move.b D7, ($2b,A0)", 0121E2 "move.b D7, ($2b,A0)"); nothing reads it
scoped object rock_soldier 2B players u8
# bit 7 when one of its gun blasts hit a turtle (0120A0 "move.b #$80, ($2c,A6)"): after the burst's least time that ends
# the burst (011884 "tst.b ($2c,A0)", 011888 "bmi $118b2"); cleared as a burst or a missile starts
# (011C78 "clr.b ($2c,A0)", 0124BC "clr.b ($2c,A0)")
scoped object rock_soldier 2C shot_hit u8
# 0x80 when it is struck (0118EC "move.b #$80, ($2d,A0)"), cleared when it recovers or its attack ends
# (0119BC "clr.b ($2d,A0)", 0118E2 "clr.b ($2d,A0)"); nothing reads it
scoped object rock_soldier 2D hurt u8
# the turtle close by it strikes (find_close_turtle's bits, bit 7 when the turtle is on its left:
# 01173E "move.b D0, ($2e,A0)"), kept while it turns to it (011CBA "tst.b ($2e,A0)", 011CC2 "ori.b #$40, ($0,A0)",
# 011CCE "clr.b ($2e,A0)")
scoped object rock_soldier 2E close_turtle u8
# the explosions so far when it is defeated, 10 in all (011A5C "addq.b #1, ($2f,A0)", 011A60 "cmpi.b #$a, ($2f,A0)"):
# boss_start_explosion places each one by it (010EF0 "move.b ($2f,A0), D7"); cleared as each move starts
# (011D40 "clr.b ($2f,A0)")
scoped object rock_soldier 2F explosions u8
# frames counted down: the waits of its way in (01160E "move.b #$50, ($30,A0)", 01167C "move.b #$28, ($30,A0)"), the
# burst's length (011C8C "move.b (A6,D7.w), ($30,A0)", 011870 "subq.b #1, ($30,A0)"), the flinch
# (01193A "move.b #$1c, ($30,A0)", 0119B0 "subq.b #1, ($30,A0)"), the defeat's steps (011A0A "move.b #$64, ($30,A0)",
# 011A24 "move.b #$c, ($30,A0)", 011A70 "move.b #$96, ($30,A0)"), when the rubble falls (011A80 "move.b ($30,A0), D7")
scoped object rock_soldier 30 timer u8
# frames its move lasts: a walk or a stand by chance (011DE6 "move.b (A6,D7.w), ($31,A0)",
# 0117BC "subq.b #1, ($31,A0)"), the jump and its landing (011D8E "move.b #$28, ($31,A0)",
# 011848 "subq.b #1, ($31,A0)"), the least a burst fires (011C92 "move.b #$20, ($31,A0)", 011878 "subq.b #1, ($31,A0)")
scoped object rock_soldier 31 move_time u8

# the rock soldier that fired it (01200A "move.l A0, ($20,A6)"): told when the blast hits
# (01209C "movea.l ($20,A0), A6", 0120A0 "move.b #$80, ($2c,A6)")
scoped object gun_blast 20 shooter u32 object.rock_soldier
# bit 7 when it flies left, the way its rock soldier faces (011FFA "ori.b #$80, ($2f,A6)", 012042 "tst.b ($2f,A0)",
# 012056 "not.w ($1a,A0)")
scoped object gun_blast 2F flies_left u8

# the rock soldier that fired it (012754 "move.l A0, ($20,A6)"); nothing reads it
scoped object missile 20 shooter u32 object.rock_soldier
# bit 7 when it flies left (012744 "ori.b #$80, ($2f,A6)", 0127A2 "tst.b ($2f,A0)", 0127B6 "not.w ($1a,A0)")
scoped object missile 2F flies_left u8

# what it goes by: the bars' (kind 4C) the rock soldier, whose defeat (routine 6) makes them go
# (0128B4 "move.l A0, ($20,A6)", 012928 "movea.l ($20,A0), A6", 01292C "cmpi.b #$6, ($4,A6)"); the hit box's (kind 4D)
# the bars, by whose routine it attacks or goes (01299C "move.l A5, ($20,A6)", 0129E2 "movea.l ($20,A0), A6",
# 0129E6 "move.b ($4,A6), D7")
scoped object shock_bars 20 leader u32 object
# the frames from one frame drawn to the next, less one: 0x3D at first, 4 less every 16 frames down to 1
# (0128E2 "move.b #$3d, ($2e,A0)", 012910 "subq.b #4, ($2e,A0)", 012914 "cmpi.b #$1, ($2e,A0)"), then one more every 8
# frames up to 0x28 when they go (01294E "addq.b #1, ($2e,A0)", 012952 "cmpi.b #$28, ($2e,A0)")
scoped object shock_bars 2E blink_period u8
# frames to the next frame drawn (012966 "subq.b #1, ($30,A0)", 01296E "move.b ($2e,A0), ($30,A0)",
# 012974 "bset #$7, ($0,A0)")
scoped object shock_bars 30 blink_timer u8

# ---- the functions ----

# -- kind 1E: the rock soldier of the building site --
# routine 0, his way in, by the state (011554 "moveq #$0, D7", 01155C "movea.l (A6,D7.w), A6": the table at 011562)
01154E  func  rock_soldier_site_enter
# state 0: drawn, his stats, the hits he takes (011576 "ori.b #$80, ($0,A0)", 01157C "lea $181cc.l, A6",
# 0115A8 "add.b D7, ($24,A0)"), standing (0115AC "movea.l $14da0.l, A6"), counted as an enemy, the boss not down and the
# area not cleared (0115D8 "addq.b #1, $6120c.l", 0115DE "clr.b $61313.l", 0115E4 "clr.b $6131d.l")
011576  func  rock_soldier_site_start
# state 1: once the scroll reaches 0x6E000 the music fades (0115EC "cmpi.l #$6e000, $63380.l",
# 0115FA "move.w #$fe, D7"), 80 frames (01160E "move.b #$50, ($30,A0)")
0115EC  func  rock_soldier_site_enter_wait_for_scroll
# state 2: after the 80 frames, his jump's animation and down at 0x800 (01161E "movea.l $14da4.l, A6",
# 01162A "move.w #$f800, ($1e,A0)")
011616  func  rock_soldier_site_enter_wait
# state 3: drops (01163C "bsr $11f94") until he is on the ground (011640 "tst.w ($10,A0)"): sound 3E, the boss music 64
# and the balloon "Crash the turtles!" beside him (011648 "move.w #$3e, D7", 011652 "move.w #$64, D7",
# 011676 "jsr $3001c.l"), 40 frames (01167C "move.b #$28, ($30,A0)")
01163C  func  rock_soldier_site_enter_drop
# state 4: the screen shakes for the 40 frames (011690 "bsr $116b0"), then he can be hit and attacks
# (011696 "ori.b #$6, ($0,A0)") and his first move (01169C "moveq #$0, D0", 01169E "bra $11c0e")
011688  func  rock_soldier_site_enter_land
# no path reaches it: the timers cleared, the next routine at its first state (0116A2 "clr.w ($30,A0)",
# 0116A6 "clr.b ($5,A0)", 0116AA "addq.b #1, ($4,A0)")
0116A2  func  rock_soldier_site_enter_end
# a layer's scroll byte (060063) from its place (063386) less 0 or 4 by the frame count (0116B0 "move.b $600a5.l, D7",
# 0116B6 "andi.b #$2, D7", 0116BC "add.b $63386.l, D7", 0116C4 "move.b D7, $60063.l"): the screen shakes
0116B0  func  rock_soldier_site_shake_screen
# routine 1: his flashing (0116CC "bsr $11f3e"); in the air or landing, the state (0116D0 "cmpi.b #$3, ($5,A0)",
# 0116DA "cmpi.b #$4, ($5,A0)"); else a turtle close by (0116E4 "bsr $11ad8") is struck at a chance from 01175A by
# blows, whether the turtle is in front and the turtles in play (0116EE "lea $1175a.l, A6",
# 011720 "move.b $61207.l, D7", 011732 "jsr $48448.l"): turned to it, sound 08, the blow's animation by the turtles in
# play and blows (011CA8 "move.w #$300, ($4,A0)", 011CD2 "move.b #$8, D7", 011CE6 "lea $11d1a.l, A6",
# 011CF4 "lea $14da0.l, A6"); else the state (011746 "lea $11782.l, A6")
0116CC  func  rock_soldier_site_think
# state 0: walks at his target (move_by_speeds within y 0x10-0x78 every other frame: 0117B8 "bsr $11f94"), aiming at it
# every 16 frames (0117A4 "bsr $11e6a"); move_time over, the move's end (0117C4 "moveq #$1, D0")
011796  func  rock_soldier_site_walk
# state 1: the same, moving two frames in four (0117DE "btst #$1, $600a5.l", 0117EA "bsr $11f94",
# 0117F6 "moveq #$2, D0")
0117CC  func  rock_soldier_site_walk_on
# state 2: stands until move_time is over (0117FE "subq.b #1, ($31,A0)", 011806 "moveq #$3, D0")
0117FE  func  rock_soldier_site_stand
# state 3: in the air, falling 0x80 faster each frame (011812 "add.w D7, ($10,A0)", 01181E "subi.w #$80, ($1e,A0)");
# down, sound 3F, on the ground with no shadow (011826 "move.w #$3f, D7", 011838 "bclr #$7, ($1,A0)")
01180E  func  rock_soldier_site_jump
# state 4: the screen shakes until move_time is over (011844 "bsr $116b0"), then he can be hit again and the move's end
# (011850 "ori.b #$2, ($0,A0)", 011856 "moveq #$4, D0")
011844  func  rock_soldier_site_jump_land
# a move over: a turtle in front within 0x8C (01185E "bsr $11b42"): the burst, routine 2, of 32 to 80 frames by chance,
# 32 at the least, the gun aimed (011C72 "move.w #$200, ($4,A0)", 011C8C "move.b (A6,D7.w), ($30,A0)",

# ---- comments ----
comment rock_soldier_site_enter the building site's rock soldier comes in, by the state of his way in
comment rock_soldier_site_start the rock soldier waits high up, his hits set by the players in play; the area is not cleared
comment rock_soldier_site_enter_wait_for_scroll once the scroll reaches him the music fades
comment rock_soldier_site_enter_wait after a while he drops
comment rock_soldier_site_enter_drop he drops to the ground, then the boss music and his balloon "Crash the turtles!"
comment rock_soldier_site_enter_land the screen shakes from his landing, then he fights
comment rock_soldier_site_enter_end Unused: ends the way in, the next routine
comment rock_soldier_site_shake_screen the screen shakes
comment rock_soldier_site_think he strikes a turtle close by at a chance, else goes on with his move
comment rock_soldier_site_walk he walks at his target, aiming at it now and then
comment rock_soldier_site_walk_on he walks on at his target
comment rock_soldier_site_stand he stands a while
comment rock_soldier_site_jump he is in the air until he lands
comment rock_soldier_site_jump_land the screen shakes from his landing, then he can be hit again
comment rock_soldier_site_move_done a move over: a burst at a turtle in front within reach, else the next move
comment rock_soldier_site_fire he fires gun blasts until the burst is over
comment rock_soldier_site_finish_attack the blow, or the gun held up after the burst, plays out; then the next move
comment rock_soldier_site_next_move the next move by chance, by what he did before
comment rock_soldier_site_walk_start he picks a turtle and walks at it, or stands if there is none
comment rock_soldier_site_walk_on_start he walks on as he was
comment rock_soldier_site_stand_start he stands a while
comment rock_soldier_site_jump_start he jumps where he stands, now and then with "Crash the turtles!"
comment rock_soldier_site_random_move_time how long the move lasts, at random
comment rock_soldier_site_weak_flash his flashing as he weakens, in his colours
comment rock_soldier_site_move he moves by his speeds within the area's depth
comment rock_soldier_technodrome_enter the Technodrome's rock soldier comes in, by the state of his way in

# ======== Baxter Stockman, the helicopters, the drones and the car (012A2E-0143BF) ========
# The kinds of the kind table (053896) whose routines are at 012A2E-0143BF. What each kind is comes from its code, its
# spawn records (area_spawn_lists: +6 the kind, +7 the parameter) and its animations, rendered from the addresses its
# set_animation calls take (the car: from the tile block it draws, with area 4's tile banks). Their stats come from
# set_object_stats' 10-byte records (+0 attack and hit, +2 health_bars, health and damage, +6 depth, +8 the hit sound).
# "Struck" is routine 4, which the attack check sets on an object a turtle's attack hits
# (0472CE "move.w #$400, ($4,A1)"); "gone off the screen" is remove_if_off_screen (flags bit 5). "With the ride" is
# carry_with_ride: in area 6 (stage 6) these objects move 0x600 a frame across with the scroll, as the knife does
# (04BB32). A smaller y is nearer the front (down the screen: Rocksteady "walks down" with
# 04F354 "addi.l #-$100, ($16,A0)"). The free objects they take are find_free_object's from object 4, 12, 24 or 32
# (062140, 0623C0, 062780, 062A00), among the next 8 or 12.
#
# kind 35 parked_car: a big car of area 4, the street of cars (one spawn record, 05E0CE). The car is a picture of 22 by
#   14 tiles the object draws into a layer (012A72 "lea $18c28.l, A6", 012A7C "jsr $183fa.l"; rendered: a sedan facing
#   the front right) and keeps where the object is by that layer's scroll (012B8C "move.w ($24,A0), $6005c.l",
#   012B94 "move.w ($26,A0), $6005e.l"); the object itself shows a piece of wall at its place (rendered 015052: a window
#   with 555-4321 under it). Once the object is under 0xE0 on the screen (012A8C "cmpi.w #$e0, ($c,A0)") the car drives
#   off to the front right for 56 frames, 4 pixels a frame (012AFE "subi.w #$4, ($24,A0)",
#   012B0A "subi.b #$4, ($27,A0)"), with three unseen hit boxes (kind 36) going the same way, the layer's rows blanked
#   one every other frame from its last row up (012BA8 "move.b #$0, (A6,D7.w)", 012BAE "move.b #$10, ($1,A6,D7.w)": the
#   high byte the colour, the low the code, tile 0x10 colour 0 being empty); then three Foot soldiers, four when 061207
#   (the turtles in play) is 2 or more, leap out of where it stood (kind 38). Harmless itself (its stats 0181A4: no
#   attack, no bars). No scenario runs the drive (index.txt: 012AA6 0 ran).
# kind 36 car_hit_box: one of the car's three unseen hit boxes (012BCC starts them: 012BD2 "move.w #$3600, ($2,A6)"), at
#   the car's place plus an offset from 012C10 by its number; not drawn (012C1C "move.b #$5, ($0,A0)": in use and
#   attacking), it moves with the car, 0x400 across and 0x400 toward the front (012C2C "move.w #$400, ($1a,A0)",
#   012C70 "sub.l D7, ($16,A0)"), knocking flying what it hits (its stats 0181E0: attack 07, damage 0x310), sound 3A as
#   each starts; its frame (01505C, rendered: a puff) only gives its attack box
# kind 38 car_soldier: a Foot soldier who leaps out of where the car stood (012C7E starts it:
#   012C84 "move.w #$3800, ($2,A6)"; rendered 015092: a Foot soldier in mid leap) to the front right until his screen y
#   is under the one of his number, then is a gun soldier (kind 09: 012D18 "move.l #$81000900, ($0,A0)",
#   enemy_gun_soldier_start)
#
# kind 43 helicopter: a small helicopter of area 6, the highway on skateboards (87 spawn records: parameter 00 16 times,
#   01 32, 80 39; with kind 69 the area's only enemies): rendered 0152F6 and 015320, the same helicopter in two colours
#   (palettes 0E and 0A by the parameter's bit 0): a rotor over a small cabin on skids. In the air with its shadow, 0x40
#   high and bobbing, it keeps in front of the turtles for 900 frames, drifting back and forth in depth, then falls
#   behind and is gone; by the parameter, bit 0 clear: bursts of four bullets (kind 44) fired down at a slant; set:
#   three missiles (kind 46) dropped; bit 7: it faces right. Four bars, attack 07 (it knocks flying the turtles it
#   touches); destroyed, a big explosion (kind 32). Sound 0A plays while any helicopter is about

#   small bullet with a trail, slanting down), 0x500 across and 0x500 down from in front of the helicopter's cabin,
#   knocking turtles down (attack 04); on the road a spark (rendered 015396), harmless, then gone
# kind 46 falling_missile: a missile that drops straight down and explodes on the ground (rendered 0153CE and 01534E: a
#   missile; the explosion is the rocket's, 01525C): parameter 0 the helicopter's (01327A starts it), knocking down

# ######## batch 3 of the names: every function of the 68000 program ########
# ======== the boot (001000-00193D) ========
# The reset: the boot screen, the RAM and ROM check (no stack: the routines come back by a jump through a register),
# then the work RAM, the DIP switches and the main loop.
# the reset (vector 1): the chips' registers cleared (00108A "bsr $10bc", 00109A "bsr $10d2"), the RAM test (00106E "jmp
# $1492.l"), the cross hatch (001170-00118A), the work RAM zeroed (0011BE "movem.l D1-D6/A1-A2, -(A0)"), the queues
# (0011CC "lea $60400.l, A0", 0011FC "lea $60380.l, A0"), the DIP switches (00122C "move.b D0, $60030.l" on), IRQ5 on
# (00138A "ori.b #$20, $60058.l") and the main loop: the fire's tiles, then each job of the queue (0013C2 "jsr $1fdca.l",
# 0013B6 "lea $13de.l, A0", 0013C0 "jsr (A0)")
001000  func  reset
# the K051960's registers 1-3 to 0 (0010BE "move.b D7, $140001.l", 0010CA "move.b D7, $140002.l")
0010BC  func  clear_sprite_chip_registers
# the K052109's registers at 106900, 106B00, 106E00 and 106C00 to 0 (0010D4 "move.b D7, $106900.l", 0010E6 "move.b D7,
# $106c00.l")
0010D2  func  clear_tile_chip_registers
# the tile RAM: the fixed layer's 0x800 tiles (0010F4 "lea $100000.l, A0", 0010FA "move.w #$7ff, D7") and the two
# layers' 0x2000 (00110C "lea $102000.l, A0") to tile 0x10, the blank one; the layers' scroll registers to 0 (001120
# "move.b D0, $106402.l")
0010EE  func  clear_tile_ram
# D1-D6, A1 and A2 to 0, for the movem that zeroes the work RAM (0011BC "bsr $114c", 0011BE "movem.l D1-D6/A1-A2,
# -(A0)")
00114C  func  zero_boot_fill_registers
# the boot screen: one palette of 16 colours into the first 16 palettes (001712 "lea $191e.l, A1", 00171C "move.b
# (A1)+, ($1,A6)"), the rest black (001730 "lea $80400.l, A6"), the fixed layer blank, and "RAM ROM CHECK" (001776
# "move.w #$0, D3", 00177A "jmp $18e2.l")
001708  func  start_boot_screen
# the 4 hexadecimal digits of D4 written backwards at A4 (001788 "andi.w #$f, D6", 001794 "addi.w #$7, D6", 001798
# "move.b D6, -(A4)"): the program chips' sums when one is bad (00156A "move.w (A0)+, D4", 001572 "jmp $1782.l"); no
# scenario has a bad chip
001782  func  print_boot_hex
# a RAM tested by bytes: 0, 0x55, 0xAA and 0xFF written and read back at each even and odd byte (0017B2 "move.b D1,
# (A1)", 0017C0 "move.b D1, ($1,A1)", 0017EE "addi.b #$55, D1"), a bad one's bits from A2 into D7 (0017BC "or.b
# ($0,A2), D7"): the tile RAM, the work RAM and the sprite RAM (0014B4 "lea $100000.l, A0", 0014DA "lea $60000.l, A0",
# 0014FE "lea $140400.l, A0")
0017A6  func  test_ram
# the same for the palette RAM, whose bytes are every other one (001806 "move.b D1, ($1,A1)", 001818 "move.b D1,
# ($3,A1)"; 00149A "lea $80000.l, A0")
0017F6  func  test_palette_ram
# the check's results: the screen cleared, "RAM ROM CHECK" and the chips' "OK" (0018AE "move.w #$1, D3"), then a "BAD"
# for each bit of D7 (0018C8 "lsr.l #1, D6", 0018CE "lea $18d8.l, A4", 0018D4 "bra $18e2")
001890  func  show_boot_check
# the text D3 of the boot's table (0018E2 "lea $15ac.l, A6"): 16-bit offsets into the fixed layer (0018FA "adda.w
# (A5)+, A6"), its characters less 0x30 (00190C "subi.b #$30, D4"), '/' a new place, '?' the end; it comes back by
# A4 (00191C "jmp (A4)")
0018E2  func  print_boot_text

# ======== the test mode's mask ROM check (001942-001E97) ========
# the exceptions' handler (the vectors' other entries): it loops until the watchdog resets the board (00193E "nop",
# 001940 "bra $193e")
00193E  func  exception_hang
# test page 1, MASK ROM CHECK, by its steps (001942 "lea $1958.l, A6", 001948 "move.b $60007.l, D7")
001942  func  mask_rom_check_page
# its first step: the three layers cleared (job 0 with 7: 001972 "move.w #$7, D7", 001976 "jsr $4164.l")
00196C  func  mask_rom_check_clear
# "MASK ROM CHECK" (00198E "move.w #$8, D7", 001992 "jsr $22aa.l") and the test's palette (001998 "lea $a07e.l, A6")
001984  func  draw_mask_rom_check
# the sums at 063500 cleared and the job that works them out queued (0019BC "lea $63500.l, A0", 0019CE "move.w
# #$1100, D7")
0019AE  func  start_mask_rom_sums
# the six sums against the right ones (0019F8 "lea $1e34.l, A0", 001A0E "cmp.w (A6)+, D7"): "OK", or each chip's "OK"
# and a "BAD" for the wrong ones (001A22 "move.w #$9, D7", 001A32 "move.w #$a, D7", 001A40 "move.w #$b, D1"); then
# 0x80 frames (0019F0 "move.b #$80, $60004.l")
0019E0  func  show_mask_rom_check
# the next page when the 0x80 frames run out (001A64 "subq.b #1, $60004.l", 001A6E "addq.b #1, $60005.l"), the
# buttons as on every page (001A7A "bra $5da4")
001A5A  func  mask_rom_check_wait

# ======== the frame (003B5C-00467B) ========

# 003C36 "move.b #$86, D7")

comment reset the board's start: the RAM and ROM check, the work RAM, the DIP switches, then the main loop that runs the queued jobs
comment clear_sprite_chip_registers the sprite chip's registers cleared
comment clear_tile_chip_registers the tile chip's registers cleared
comment clear_tile_ram the three tile layers blank and their scroll at 0
comment zero_boot_fill_registers zeroes for the boot's clearing of the work RAM
comment start_boot_screen the boot's screen: a palette, the fixed layer blank and "RAM ROM CHECK"
comment print_boot_hex a number as four hexadecimal digits, for a bad program chip's sum
comment test_ram a RAM written and read back with four patterns, its bad chips marked
comment test_palette_ram the palette RAM written and read back with four patterns
comment show_boot_check the check's results: each chip OK or BAD
comment print_boot_text a text of the boot's screen
comment exception_hang an exception: the program stops until the watchdog resets the board
comment mask_rom_check_page the test mode's mask ROM check
comment mask_rom_check_clear the layers cleared for the mask ROM check
comment draw_mask_rom_check the mask ROM check's heading and palette
comment start_mask_rom_sums the mask ROMs' sums started
comment show_mask_rom_check each mask ROM's sum shown OK or BAD
comment mask_rom_check_wait the results shown a while, then the next page
comment sum_mask_roms the graphics ROMs summed through the video chips
comment sum_sprite_roms_low the sprite ROMs' first half summed
comment sum_sprite_roms_high the sprite ROMs' second half summed
comment sum_sprite_rom_banks the sprite ROMs' banks read through the sprite chip and summed
comment sum_tile_roms the tile ROMs read through the tile chip and summed
comment add_to_rom_sums four bytes of a graphics ROM added to its sums
comment clear_layers_job the tile layers chosen cleared
comment blank_tile the blank tile and its colour
comment clear_fixed_layer the fixed layer blank
comment clear_scroll_layer a scrolling layer blank
comment print_table_text a text of a table of texts into the fixed layer, or erased
comment set_text_colour the colour of the texts printed next
comment set_spare_text_colour a second texts' colour no text uses
comment add_point an enemy defeated: a point to the players' scores, the top score kept
comment add_point_to_score a point to a player's score and the top score kept
comment draw_scores the chosen players' scores drawn in their boxes
comment draw_score_player_1 the first player's score in his box
comment draw_score_player_2 the second player's score in his box
comment draw_score_player_3 the third player's score in his box
comment draw_score_player_4 the fourth player's score in his box
comment draw_top_score the top score after HIGH
comment draw_score_digits a score's four digits, without leading zeros
comment draw_blank_digit a blank in place of a leading zero
comment draw_digit a digit of a score
comment clear_scores the chosen scores to 0
comment print_plain_text a short text in the plain colour
comment draw_score_labels unused: the labels 1UP to 4UP and the top score
comment print_colour_text a text of the test mode's and the credits' table, in its own colour
comment draw_tile_picture unused: a picture of rows of tiles
comment draw_player_boxes the chosen players' boxes, and their scores
comment draw_player_box a player's box: its frame and label, its lives, its health bar
comment draw_box_frame_and_label a player's box frame and label in his colour
comment draw_lives a player's lives in his box
comment draw_health_bar a player's health bar in his box
comment player_box_colour a player's colour in the boxes
comment clear_lives_digits the lives' place in a box blank
comment clear_health_bar the health bar's place in a box blank
comment draw_box_frame a player's box frame
comment draw_box_label a player's box label 1UP to 4UP
comment print_stage_title unused: the stage's number and its name of the development
comment draw_player_message the message under a player's box
comment message_insert_coin INSERT COIN(S) in a player's box
comment message_press_start PRESS START blinking under a player's box
comment message_out_of_lives the knocked-out head of a player who lost his last life
comment message_clear the line under a player's box cleared
comment big_character_colour the colour of a big character
comment print_tall_text a text in tall characters: the rankings, CONTINUE, GAME OVER
comment draw_tall_character a tall character
comment erase_tall_character a tall character erased
comment tall_text_colour the colour of a text in tall characters
comment update_coins the coins: the coin counters, the coins inserted turned into credits
comment new_coin_presses the coin switches just pressed, with the coin's sound
comment pulse_coin_counter a coin slot's counter pulsed for each coin
comment count_coin a coin inserted, counted towards the slot's credits
comment add_credit_lives each slot's credits added to its player's lives
comment vblank_interrupt the frame's interrupt: the inputs, the coins, the sound, the palettes and the game state's frame
comment read_inputs the coins and the four players' inputs read, and the layers' scroll written
comment run_startup the steps after the reset
comment startup_begin the video chips set, the test mode when its switch is on, else the screen cleared
comment startup_wait the screen cleared
comment startup_end on to the attract mode
comment set_screen_flip the screen flipped by its DIP switch
comment run_attract the attract mode's frame, and a game when a player starts
comment run_game the game's frame by its scene
comment run_test_mode the test mode's frame
comment queue_job a job into the main loop's queue

# ======== the game's scenes (0061CE-006BE3) ========
# Game state 2, the game, runs the scene (060005) by the table at 00413A (00412E "lea $413a.l, A0"): 0 a new game, 1 the
# players' turtles, 2 an area's set-up, 3 its story and title screens, 4 the play, 5 the area's exit, 6 the ending, 7 the
# continue, 8 the ranking. Each scene runs its steps (060007, then 060009 and 06000B) by tables of its own, and most
# steps wait for the jobs they queue (060082) and the palette requests under way (060083). The demo runs scenes 1, 2, 3
# and 5-7 by a table of its own (attract_demo: 004CBC "lea $4cd2.l, A6"); 0600C2 is the scenes' frame counter.

# ======== the ranking (007B0C-0088BF) ========
# The ranking in work RAM: 99 scores and the new one (BCD words 063500-0635C7: reset_ranking copies 0x32 longs) and the

# the initial each enters 0635FA-0635FD (3 done), the players entering 0635FE, their buttons held 0635FF, and 0634A0
# set when a name was entered. 0635F8 is a frame counter, and before that the turtles left to draw in black.

# ======== the layers' maps, the code (01E050-01FDC9) ========
# The areas' two tile layers, the K052109's layer A (tile RAM 102000) and layer B (104000), keep 64 bytes each at 063340
# (A) and 063380 (B): x and y (24.8), the speeds (+0C, +0E), the map, its blocks and width (+12, +16, +10), and the row
# and the column the scroll has brought into view (+30 and +34 set by queue_scroll_row: 01B526 "subq.b #1, $63334.l";
# +2C and +35 by auto_scroll: 01AD46 "subq.b #1, $63335.l"). The code works on a copy at 063300: load, draw, save.
# The floor map (061800, 0x40 cells a row) gets walls (FF, and FE or FD where a wall blocks one side: turtle_wall_contacts
# 01D774 "cmpi.b #-$2, D1" right, 01D7A0 "cmpi.b #-$3, D1" left) and floor (01).

# ---- the whole layers and the working copy ----
# the whole layer at A0 (8 rows of 16 blocks: 01E082 "moveq #$8, D7", 01E084 "moveq #$10, D6") from the working layer's
# map and blocks (01E074 "movea.l $63312.l, A2", 01E08C "movea.l $63316.l, A4"), and each block's floor cells into the
# floor map (01E07C "lea $61800.l, A1", 01E0AA "move.b ($1,A4), ($0,A1)"; the tiles from +11: 01E0C2 "move.b ($11,A4),
# ($1,A0)"): the street's and the building site's starts (01E3EC "bsr $1e050", 01E550 "bsr $1e050")
01E050  func  draw_whole_layer_and_floor
# the same without the floor map: each block's colour byte to the even addresses, its tile codes to the odd ones

01E11E  func  draw_whole_layer

# ======== the object engine (046EEA-047D97, src/engine/sprites.c) ========
# the 128 sprites of the K051960's sprite RAM off, each with its own priority (046EEA "lea $140400.l, A0", 046EF2 "moveq
# #$4f, D1", 046EF4 "move.b D1, ($0,A0)", 046EFA "andi.b #$7f, D1": bit 7, shown, clear); the scenes' and the areas'
# starts (006846 "jsr $46eea.l")
046EEA  func  hide_all_sprites
# every frame: each object drawn into the draw list at 061400 by screen_y + depth + 0x38 (046F30 "move.w ($34,A0), D0",
# 046F38 "addi.w #$38, D0"), the objects of a row linked by draw_next (046F66 "move.w A0, ($3e,A2)"), the first row and
# the count (046F72 "move.w D5, $61204.l", 046F78 "move.b D6, $61206.l"); one out of the list (0x180 or more) or not
# drawn has its animation stepped on all the same (046F8C "bsr $471ae")
046F08  func  build_draw_list
# the attack check, every frame (006938 "jsr $47204.l"): the turtles' attacks against half the objects 4-39, every other
# one by frame_count (04720A "btst #$0, $600a5.l", 047318 "adda.w #$a0, A1"), those objects' attacks against the turtles
# (047342 "lea $62000.l, A1"), and two of the objects 4-11 (attack_check_objects: 04742E "lea $471f4.l, A0") against the
# objects 12-23 (047450 "lea $623c0.l, A1"); a hit when the attack box (the frame's, attack_depth not negative: 047232
# "tst.w ($8,A2)") meets the body box: routine 4 (0472CE "move.w #$400, ($4,A1)"), the hit, the damage off the health,
# and an enemy defeated by a turtle credited to its player (0472FE "move.w #$400, D7", 04730C "jsr $4164.l")
047204  func  check_attacks
# turtle_collide (01AB7E "jsr $47534.l"): the turtle against the objects 4-11 by the body boxes (047534 "lea $62140.l,
# A3", 04753A "moveq #$7, D7"): a side blocked into its contacts (047632 "or.b D1, ($1,A0)"), on top of one (0475F2
# "ori.b #$10, ($0,A0)", 047600 "move.b D0, ($32,A0)"), carried by one whose kind has bit 7 (04760E "tst.b ($2,A3)",
# 04761C "add.l D2, ($12,A0)")
047534  func  turtle_collide_with_objects
# the same for an enemy (enemy_think 048B56 "jsr $47662.l", enemy_react 048EE6 "jsr $47662.l"), keeping its contacts'
# top 3 bits (04766A "andi.b #$e0, ($1,A0)") and never carried
047662  func  enemy_collide_with_objects
# the area's start (006840 "jsr $4776e.l"): the players' slots at 062FA0 given their turtles (04776E "move.l #$62000,
# $62fa0.l") and cleared (04779C "movem.l D0-D2, $62fa4.l"), the first slot and turtle the nearest (0477BC "move.l
# #$62fa0, $61226.l", 0477C6 "move.l #$62000, $6122e.l"), a byte by the area into 06124C (0477D0 "lea $48830.l, A6")
04776E  func  start_player_slots
# the object loop, every frame (006932 "jsr $477ea.l"): the enemies' spawns (0477EA "jsr $47a32.l"), the players' slots
# (0477F6 "bsr $4783c"), and every object in use of 4-39 (0477FA "lea $62140.l, A0", 047832 "cmpa.l #$62c80, A0") runs
# its kind's routine (047812 "lea $53896.l, A6", 04781E "move.b ($4,A0), D0", 047828 "jsr (A6)") and gets its screen
# place (04782A "bsr $4789c")
0477EA  func  run_objects
# each slot whose turtle is in use (04784A "tst.b (A5)"): enemy_behind cleared (047850 "clr.b ($44,A5)") and counted;
# the slot with the fewest enemies so far into 061208 (047862 "move.l A6, $61208.l"), its grab_time counted down
# (047870 "subq.b #1, ($8,A6)"); the turtles in play into 061207, and the enemies about (06120C) shared among them, at
# least 1, into 06120D (04788E "divu.w D1, D0", 047894 "move.b D0, $6120d.l")
04783C  func  update_player_slots
# its screen place from its place in the area and the spawn scroll (0478A8 "move.l $61218.l, D1", 0478B4 "addi.w #$1a0,
# D0", 0478C0 "move.l $6121c.l, D3", 0478CC "addi.w #$100, D2"), and flags bit 5 when it is off the screen by the
# margins spawn_offsets has for its kind (0478D4 "bclr #$5, ($0,A0)", 0478DA "lea $53a5e.l, A4", 0478EE "cmpi.w #$1c0,
# D0")
04789C  func  update_object_screen_place
# A6 = the first free object (flags 0) of the group D0 picks, from object_groups and object_group_counts (047C02 "lea
# $47bde.l, A6", 047C12 "lea $47be2.l, A6", 047C1E "tst.b ($0,A6)"); Z set when there is one
047C02  func  take_free_object_in_group
# an object from the record in A5 (x, y and height from the object in A0, then its group, kind and parameter): in use,
# routine 0, its own colours, nothing a turtle throws (047C30 "move.b ($5,A5), D0", 047C3A "move.w #$100, ($0,A6)",

# ---- the fade (copy_palette_sets' steps, by 063411) ----
# The palette RAM's parts in 063418's mask (5 of them: 00975C's table, 080000, 080800, 080A00, 080400, 080600) are read
# into a buffer at 063800, moved toward the target sets a step, and written back, a part a frame; a caller that goes on
# calling copy_palette_sets fades in (the opening: attract frames 40-250 go from dark to the city)
# step 0: the fade starts: its mask and step (00965C "move.w D6, $63418.l"), the target sets (009662 "move.l A5,
# $63414.l"), the buffer (009668 "lea $63800.l, A5")
009642  func  fade_palettes_start
# step 1: a part of the palette RAM into the buffer (0096A2 "move.b ($1,A6), (A5)+", 0096A6 "move.b ($3,A6), (A5)+"), the
# next step after the fifth (0096BE "cmpi.b #$5, $63412.l", 0096CA "addq.b #1, $63411.l")
009678  func  fade_palettes_read
# step 2: a part's colours in the buffer a step toward the target set's (009778 "move.b $63419.l, D0": the step, 009782
# "movea.l $63414.l, A5")
009770  func  fade_palettes_step
# a colour's red, green or blue (009872's masks: 1F, 3E0, 7C00) moved toward the target's by the step, no further
009838  func  fade_colour_part
# step 3: the buffer back into a part of the palette RAM (009714 "move.b (A5)+, ($1,A6)", 009718 "move.b (A5)+, ($3,A6)");
# after the fifth the fade's step is over (00973C "clr.l $63410.l")
0096EA  func  fade_palettes_write
# the part's palette RAM address (009744 "lea $975c.l, A6", 00974C "movea.l (A6,D7.w), A6"), 128 colours (009750 "move.w
# #$7f, D7"), the buffer's place (009754 "movea.l $6341a.l, A5")
009744  func  fade_palettes_part
comment fade_palettes_start a fade toward a set of palettes starts
comment fade_palettes_read a part of the palettes read into the fade's buffer
comment fade_palettes_step a part of the fade's colours a step toward the target palettes
comment fade_colour_part a colour's red, green or blue a step toward the target's
comment fade_palettes_write the fade's colours written back into a part of the palettes
comment fade_palettes_part where a part of the palettes is and how many colours it has

# an arc an enemy jumps or falls on: its speed across (04863E "move.w (A6), ($1a,A0)"), what slows it each frame until
# it would turn (048696 "move.w ($2,A6), D0", 0486AE "bpl $486b6"), its speed in height (048646 "move.w ($4,A6), ($1e,A0)"),
# what pulls that down each frame (0486B6 "move.w ($6,A6), D0") as far as a limit (0486BE "cmp.w ($a,A6), D0"), and a
# step across it takes at once (04864C "move.w ($8,A6), D7", 048690 "add.l D7, ($12,A0)"), all mirrored when it faces left

field arc 02 x_drag s16
field arc 04 height_speed s16

param enemy_arc_step a6 arc arc

# ---- the boot (system/boot.c) ----
# the coinage by the DIP switches' coin settings: two bytes a setting, the coins (00126E "lea $1452.l, A0", 001274
# "move.b (A0,D1.w), $60303.l") and the credits they give (00127C "move.b ($1,A0,D1.w), $60304.l"); the test mode shows
# them (005C90 "lea $1452.l, A6")
001452  table  coinage_coins  u8
001453  table  coinage_credits  u8
# the second coin slot's, by the bank's high bits (00128A "lea $1472.l, A0", 001290 "move.b (A0,D2.w), $6030b.l",
# 001298 "move.b ($1,A0,D2.w), $6030c.l")
001472  table  coinage_2_coins  u8
001473  table  coinage_2_credits  u8
# the lives a credit gives by the DIP switches (0012AC "lea $1426.l, A0"; the test mode, 005D16 "lea $1426.l, A6"): 1,
# 2, 3 or 5
001426  table  lives_settings  u8
# the unused DIP settings: four records of 10 bytes by dip_switches_2's bits 3-4 (0012DC "andi.b #$18, D0", 0012E4
# "add.w D1, D0"), a flag and two longs the reset copies (0012EE "move.w (A0)+, D0", 0012FC "move.l (A0)+, (A1)+",
# 0012FE "move.l (A0), (A1)")
00142A  data  unused_dip_settings
struct dip_setting 0A rom
field dip_setting 00 flag u16
field dip_setting 02 value u32
field dip_setting 06 value_2 u32
local reset 0012EC a0 setting dip_setting
# the boot's texts by their number (0018E2 "lea $15ac.l, A6", then the text's address by D3): RAM CHECK, ROM CHECK...
0015AC  table  boot_texts  u32  text
# the program's chips the ROM test sums: where each starts and how many blocks of 4 KB it has (001856 "lea $16cc.l, A0",
# 00185C "move.l (A0)+, D6", 001864 "move.w (A0)+, D0"), up to a negative start (00185E "bmi $188e")
0016CC  data  program_chips
struct program_chip 06 rom
field program_chip 00 start u32
field program_chip 04 blocks u16
local sum_program_chips 001856 a0 chip program_chip
# the sums good chips give, which the reset compares (001524 "lea $16f8.l, A3", 001530 "cmp.w (A3)+, D6")
0016F8  data  good_chip_sums
struct chip_sum 02 rom
field chip_sum 00 sum u16
local reset 001524 a3 expected chip_sum
# where the reset prints a bad chip's sum (00155E "lea $16e8.l, A1", 001568 "movea.l (A1)+, A4", then print_boot_hex)
0016E8  data  chip_sum_places
struct text_place 04 rom
field text_place 00 place u32 io
local reset 00155E a1 place text_place
# the boot's colours: 16 colours of two bytes each (001712 "lea $191e.l, A1", 00171C "move.b (A1)+, ($1,A6)", 001720
# "move.b (A1)+, ($3,A6)"), into each of the 16 palettes
00191E  data  boot_colours
struct palette_colour 02 rom
field palette_colour 00 high u8
field palette_colour 01 low u8
local start_boot_screen 001712 a1 colour palette_colour

comment direction_to the direction from the object to a place on the screen, from its quadrant and the angle table
comment draw_sprites every frame: the draw list's objects into the sprite chip with their shadows, their animations stepped on, the rest turned off
comment step_animation the object's animation stepped on to its next frame when the frame's time runs out, without drawing it
comment set_animation starts an animation on the object: its first frame, timed by the frame's count plus the object's animation delay
comment speeds_from_direction_unscaled Unused: speeds_from_direction's work without its last shift: the speeds across and up or down of a byte's speed in a direction, 256 times larger
comment lone_return_before_krang_explode_next Unused: an empty routine that returns at once
comment start_area_spawns the area's spawn list, the speeds and directions of its spawn scroll and where that scroll starts
comment spawn_enemies every frame: the spawn scroll moved on and, when it reaches the next record, its enemy put into a free object

comment spawn_offset the screen margin a spawn record's kind of enemy comes in from
comment take_free_object the first free object of the group a spawn record picks, and whether there is one
comment run_object_state the object's current state run from the table of state handlers it is given
comment move_object_with_height the object moved by its speeds, its height too
comment move_object the object moved by its speeds across and up or down

comment move_object_blocked the object moved by its speeds, but not into a side its contacts say is blocked

# the window a diving soldier breaks: its two places and their tile blocks (04CDBA "move.b (A5), D7", 04CDBE "movea.l

# ---- batch 8a2: what the routines leave in registers for later ones to read, kept as the game's state ----
# A part of a register a routine reads before anything sets it is what the code before left there: all through the
# frame from the VBLANK handler down, which finds the registers of the code it interrupted (003DC4 "movem.l
# D0-D7/A0-A6, $60440.l", put back at 003E44 "movem.l $60440.l, D0-D7/A0-A6"). Those parts, and every value that
# reaches them, are global variables of the C (core/decompiler/carried.py; the runtime puts them back when an
# interrupt's handler returns); the rest of each register stays in the functions' locals and parameters.
# 00FCE8 "move.w #$2000, D7" 00FCFA "add.l D7, ($12,A6)" hydrant_start_water adds all of D7 to the water's x having set
# only its low word: the high word is what the routines before left (00EBD2 krang_start_fist, 048690 enemy_start_arc,
# the billboard's soldier, the rock soldier's blast, the Technodrome's missile do the same); 002338 "btst D6, D7"
# 009362 "btst D6, D7" the boxes and the palette requests test bits of D7 as a long
register d7 offset_high_word
comment offset_high_word the high word of what the code adds as an offset or tests as a long of flags in D7, whose low word only it sets: 0 after a count, a sound or a mask of its own (a moveq), FFFF where an enemy has not landed (enemy_landed 04863A "moveq #-$1, D7"), the sign of a step across (enemy_start_arc 048674 "ext.l D7"), what is left of a product (random_below 04847C "swap D7")
# 03028A "cmpi.w #$130, D1" show_balloon takes D1's word for the speaker's x on the screen, 046FFC "cmpi.w #$1a0, D1"
# draw_sprites for a sprite's x, and the area exits for a turtle's (02CE00 "move.w D1, ($c,A0)"): its high byte, and
# the high word over it, are what the routines before left where they set only its low byte
register d1 screen_x_high
comment screen_x_high the high byte of the word the code takes for an x on the screen in D1, and the high word above it: what the area exits' routines put there for a speed or a place (turtle_exit_go_to_place 02CE0C "lsl.l #8, D1"), the high byte of a tile offset (draw_box_frame), of a job's word (the main loop), of a scroll step (auto_scroll 01ACEE "lsl.w #5, D1")
# 047DD0 "exg D1, D2" direction_to swaps the distances across and up and down, and reads D2's high word with the one
# across (the area exits' turtle_exit_go_to_place 02CE0E "lsl.l #8, D2" left a place in it)
register d2 distance_high_word
comment distance_high_word the high word of D2, which direction_to reads with a distance across after swapping it with D1: what the area exits leave there (a turtle's place times 256, turtle_exit_go_to_place 02CE0E "lsl.l #8, D2")
# 013078 "tst.b D5" helicopter_fly takes D5's low byte for whether the turtle it aims at is in line, set only where it
# finds one (013006 "moveq #$1, D5"); 00E890 "move.w ($e,A6), D5" 00E89E "cmpi.w #$b, D5" the routines that look for a
# turtle close by work out a distance in D5's word and leave its low byte; 003D4E "abcd D5, D4" add_credit_lives adds
# it to the lives
register d5 distance_low_byte
comment distance_low_byte the low byte of the distance up and down or across that the routines that look for a turtle close by work out in D5 (krang_find_close_turtle 00E89E "cmpi.w #$b, D5") and leave there; helicopter_fly takes it for whether a turtle is in line, the tile drawers for a tile's colour, add_credit_lives for the lives a credit adds
# 00965C "move.w D6, $63418.l" fade_palettes_start keeps D6 for the fade's banks and rate; 0024AC "move.b ($1,A4,D6.w),
# D0" player_box_colour reads D6's word for the player's number, whose high byte the routines before left
register d6 fade_banks
comment fade_banks D6's low word: the banks and the rate of a fade (fade_palettes_start 00965C "move.w D6, $63418.l": the ending's and the opening's fades put them there), the bank a palette request reached (palette_request_area), the board's control byte send_sound_command writes (00923A "move.b D6, $a0001.l"); the players' boxes read its high byte as the high byte of the player's number
# 0095EA "move.b (A4)+, ($1,A5)" copy_palette_list writes colours where A5 points, 009662 "move.l A5, $63414.l"
# fade_palettes_start keeps it for the palettes to fade to; 0094AC "movea.l (A5,D6.w), A5" the palette requests set it
# to a bank's place in the palette RAM and leave it for the next request
register a5 palette_place
comment palette_place where A5 points in the palettes: the place in the palette RAM a palette request copies colours to (palette_request_list 0094AC "movea.l (A5,D6.w), A5", copy_palette_list moves it on), the palettes a fade goes to (fade_palettes_start 009662 "move.l A5, $63414.l": the ending's and the opening's fades put them there)

# ---- batch 8b: what the object loop hands each object's routine in a register, kept as the game's state ----
# 0477F6 "bsr $4783c" run_objects starts with A5 where update_player_slots leaves it (047848 "movea.l (A6), A5": the
# last slot's turtle) and runs each object's routine with it, 047828 "jsr (A6)"; a routine that leaves A5 elsewhere
# hands that to the next object's (the bosses' aims leave their target, boss_direction_to_target 0184D2 "movea.l
# ($20,A0), A5"; the enemies that look for a slot leave the second nearest, enemy_think)
register a5 object_loop_leftover run_objects
comment object_loop_leftover what the object loop's routines leave in A5 for the next one: the last slot's turtle where the loop starts (update_player_slots), a boss's target (boss_direction_to_target), the second nearest slot an enemy found (enemy_think)


# ======== batch 8b-mem: the pointers the C reached memory through by address, with their types ========
# What the code walks or reads through a pointer, typed: the board's memories (u32 io: the bus, as the original), the
# work RAM's records and arrays (a structure; an array a pointer walks is a record of one field, which the C reads and
# writes: ELEMENT macros are const), the program's records (rom). The types of the lines above that were already
# there are marked "type:" in the comment over each.

# ---- the work RAM's arrays a pointer walks, one record an element ----
# a player's input byte: turtle_inputs (060020: what it holds, the stick's bits 0-3, jump 0x10, attack 0x20),
# turtle_presses (06004C: what it has just pressed), player_inputs (060034: the inputs read this frame); the turtles'
# routines take theirs in A1 and A2 from turtle_run_all (01A43A "lea $60020.l, A1", 01A440 "lea $6004c.l, A2",
# 01A554 "addq.l #1, A1")
struct player_input 01
field player_input 00 bits u8
# a player's marker timer, a byte of marker_times (061100): counted down every frame (01A34C "subq.b #1, (A6)")
struct marker_timer 01
field marker_timer 00 frames u8
# a cell of floor_map (061800, 0x40 cells a row): what is at a place of the area (01DEB4 "lea $61800.l, A6", 01DEC0
# "move.b (A6), $633d3.l"); the layers' setups write four at a time (01E30E "move.l D0, (A0)+")
struct floor_map_cell 01
field floor_map_cell 00 cell u8
# a slot of job_queue (060380): a job and its parameter, 0xFFFF when empty (004164 "movea.l $60010.l, A6", 00416A
# "move.w D7, (A6)+"; 00139E "move.w #$ffff, (A0)+")
struct queued_job 02
field queued_job 00 job u16
# a slot of sound_queue (060400): a command for the sound board (0091DA "move.b D7, (A6)+", 009212 "move.b (A6)+, D7")
struct queued_sound 01
field queued_sound 00 command u8
# a byte of hug_turtle_colours (0633E6): a turtle's colour in the April hug, FF once it is out (02C4EE "move.l
# #$8090a0b, (A1)", 02C506 "move.b #$ff, (A1)", 02C61A "move.b (A1)+, D0")
struct hug_colour 01
field hug_colour 00 colour u8
# a colour of the fade's buffer (063800): the palette's colours read (0096A2, a byte at a time), faded a step a frame
# (0097D4 "move.w (A6), D1", 0097EA "move.w D5, (A6)+") and written back
struct fade_colour 02
field fade_colour 00 colour u16
# a byte of it, as fade_palettes_read and fade_palettes_write copy the palette RAM's colours a byte at a time
# (0096A2 "move.b ($1,A6), (A5)+", 009714 "move.b (A5)+, ($1,A6)")
field fade_colour 00 part u8
# a sum the MASK ROM CHECK adds up in the work RAM, over the ranking's scores (0019BC "lea $63500.l, A0", 001D90
# "add.w D3, (A6)+"), compared with good_mask_rom_sums (001A0C "move.w (A0)+, D7", 001A0E "cmp.w (A6)+, D7")
struct mask_rom_total 02
field mask_rom_total 00 sum u16
# an entry of draw_list (061400): the object to draw, the low half of its address (046FBC "move.w (A1)+, D6",
# 046FC4 "movea.l D6, A0"), cleared once drawn (046FC0 "clr.w (-$2,A1)")
struct draw_entry 02
field draw_entry 00 object u16 object
# a turtle's throw timer: frames since its last throw, which turtle_attack_over reaches through turtle_throw_moves'
# records (01BFAE "movea.l ($2,A5,D0.w), A5"): the throw only at 0x100 or more, then cleared (01BFB2 "cmpi.w #$100,
# (A5)", 01BFBA "clr.w (A5)")
struct throw_timer 02
field throw_timer 00 frames u16
# ---- the program's records ----
# an elevator's stop (elevator_stops, elevator_stops_2): the screen x it stops at and its wait there (04C716
# "movea.l ($24,A0), A1", 04C71A "move.w (A1), D0", 04C724 "move.b ($2,A1), ($46,A0)")
struct elevator_stop 04 rom
field elevator_stop 00 x u16
field elevator_stop 02 wait u8
# a window soldier's record in object_tile_blocks: the screen x it jumps out at, then the frames the window takes to
# break (high byte) and the delay between its steps (low byte), read as one word (04CC14 "move.w (A5)+, ($20,A0)",
# 04CC18 "move.w (A5)+, ($46,A0)"); its window_break_steps follow
struct window_drop 04 rom
field window_drop 00 trigger_x u16
field window_drop 02 times u16
# a diving window soldier's record in object_tile_block_pairs: the screen y it dives out at (04CD94 "move.w (A6)+,
# ($20,A0)"); its dive_window follows
struct window_dive 02 rom
field window_dive 00 trigger_y u16
# a colour channel's mask and the step a fade moves it by (009872: 001F/0001, 03E0/0020, 7C00/0400): 00983A "move.w
# (A2)+, D3" 009840 "mulu.w (A2)+, D4"
struct colour_channel 04 rom
field colour_channel 00 mask u16
field colour_channel 02 step u16
# a list of palette effects starts with how many (009884 "move.w (A6)+, D7", 009886 "subq.w #1, D7"), the pointers
# to them follow (0098A8 "movea.l (A6)+, A4")
elements palette_effect_count u16
# a palette effect's data starts with its colour code: bank, palette and colour (0098AA "move.w (A4)+, D6", 0098B4
# "andi.w #$f00, D5", 0098C4 "andi.w #$f0, D5", 0098CC "andi.w #$f, D6"), its steps follow
elements palette_effect_code u16
# the title logo's pieces' places on the screen, x and y (004B30 "move.w (A6,D7.w), ($c,A0)", 004B36 "move.w
# ($2,A6,D7.w), ($e,A0)")
elements logo_place u16
# a font's tile codes, two a character, top and bottom (0090B6 "move.b (A3,D6.w), ($1,A6)", 0090BC "move.b
# ($1,A3,D6.w), ($81,A6)")
elements font_tile u8
# where a player's box's parts are drawn in the fixed layer (player_box_places: the frame, the label, the lives, the
# health bar): 00258C "movea.l ($4,A6,D5.w), A5"
elements box_part_place u32 io
